//: Every Apple identifier this project needs to build, sign, sideload, and ship.
Copy this file to apple-project.json and replace the placeholder values with
your own. apple-project.json is gitignored: nothing in it is a secret on its
own — the actual secret is the .p8 private key, which lives outside the repo
(see appStoreConnect.privateKeyPath) — but identifiers plus a public repo is
more of a map than anyone needs.
cp apple-project.example.json apple-project.json
$EDITOR apple-project.json
scripts/xcode/gen-xcconfig.sh && xcodegen generate
Placeholders read REPLACE_ME or use the name John Smith. Values that describe
this repository rather than your account — paths.*, the string catalogs, the
App Store field limits — are already correct and can be left alone.
JSON has no comment syntax. Keys beginning with // are documentation and every
JSON parser will hand them to you as ordinary strings — ignore them by name.

team.//: Per-account. Identical across every app on this developer account.
team.//id: DEVELOPMENT_TEAM in project.yml and TEAMID in ExportOptions.plist. Apple Developer > Membership. Ten characters.
team.//name: Cosmetic — appears in certificate common names.
team.name: John Smith
team.//entity: How the seller is spelled in listings and legal copy.
team.//appleId: The account the certificates belong to. Xcode > Settings > Accounts.

app.//: Per-app. Everything here changes when you start a new project.
app.//name: CFBundleDisplayName. Under 12 characters or the home screen truncates it.
app.name: HeartRate Broadcaster
app.//bundleIdPrefix: options.bundleIdPrefix in project.yml. Reverse-DNS of a domain you control.
app.//bundleId: The App ID registered on developer.apple.com. Must match PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER exactly — a mismatch shows up as an opaque provisioning failure at archive time.
app.//extensions: Every embedded target needs its own App ID, and each must be a child of the parent bundle ID. The watch app additionally sets INFOPLIST_KEY_WKCompanionAppBundleIdentifier to the parent.
app.//appGroup: Only needed if targets share a container. This app does not use one — the widget receives state through ActivityKit, not a shared defaults suite.
app.//capabilities: Must be enabled on the App ID in the developer portal AND declared in the .entitlements file. Enabling one without the other fails at signing, not at build.
app.//deploymentTarget: iOS 26 is forced by HKLiveWorkoutBuilder, which is how AirPods Pro 3 heart rate reaches an app. Do not lower it without removing that path.
app.//deviceFamily: TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY. 1 = iPhone, 2 = iPad, 4 = Watch. Declaring iPad obliges you to supply iPad screenshots.
app.//marketingVersion: MARKETING_VERSION, the version users see. The build number auto-increments in build_number.xcconfig via a preBuildScript.

//: Where the scripts should look. Every value is relative to the repo root.
These exist so scripts/*.ts carry no project name of their own — the only
place 'HeartRateBroadcaster' appears is here and in project.yml. A new
project changes this block and nothing else. For this repository the values
below are already correct.
paths.//xcodeproj: Generated by xcodegen from project.yml, and gitignored. Named after project.yml's top-level `name`.
paths.//scheme: What -scheme takes when archiving. XcodeGen names the scheme after the target, so this is usually the app target's name.
paths.//derivedBuildDir: Where xcodebuild leaves the intermediate that scripts/lib/catalog.ts mines for extracted strings. Relative to whatever -derivedDataPath the build used.
//builds: One entry per platform that owns source. scripts/lib/catalog.ts builds each of
these with SWIFT_EMIT_LOC_STRINGS so the compiler writes the .stringsdata it
then mines. A platform missing here contributes no strings and its catalog
//stringCatalogs: Every .xcstrings in the project, in the order they should be reported.
scripts/lib/catalog.ts opens new slots in these and scripts/site/localize.ts fills
them. A catalog missing from this list is silently never translated.
`target` is the build target whose .stringsdata feeds the catalog, or null
for an InfoPlist catalog — permission prompts are written by hand and have
no Swift source to extract from, which is also why they carry
They stay one catalog per target rather than one shared file because a watch
app and a widget extension do not link the phone app's bundle, and a string
can only be looked up from the bundle it was compiled into.

stringCatalogs.//: The LiveActivity sources compile into both the app and this extension, but a Live Activity is always rendered by the extension's process, so its strings are looked up in the extension's bundle. The catalog has to live here rather than beside the code.

paths.//screenshotTarget: The UI test target that drives the simulator for App Store screenshots. Null if the project has none.

signing.//: Certificates live in the login keychain. `security find-identity -v -p codesigning` lists what is actually installed — trust that over what the portal says, and copy the identity names below from its output.
signing.//style: Automatic lets Xcode manage profiles. Manual is only worth it in CI without a keychain.
signing.//developmentIdentity: Signs builds for devices you own. Free provisioning cannot do HealthKit or background Bluetooth, so a paid account is required here.
signing.//distributionIdentity: Signs archives for the App Store and for ad-hoc sideloading.
signing.//exportMethods: Values for the `method` key in ExportOptions.plist. app-store-connect uploads or exports for the store; release-testing is the old ad-hoc, limited to UDIDs registered on the portal; debugging is development; developer-id is macOS only.

appStoreConnect.//: Only needed to upload builds. Building and sideloading to your own device needs nothing in this block.
appStoreConnect.//appleId: The numeric App ID, visible in the App Store Connect URL and in every apps.apple.com link. Not the bundle ID.
appStoreConnect.//issuerId: Per-team, per-account, and only visible in the browser at Users and Access > Integrations > App Store Connect API. There is no API that returns it. Every API key on the team shares it, and using the wrong one produces 401 NOT_AUTHORIZED — which reads exactly like a permissions problem and is not.
appStoreConnect.//keys: Uploading a build needs App Manager or Admin. Developer is enough to archive but not to upload.
appStoreConnect.//privateKeyPath: altool takes no path argument — it looks up AuthKey_<id>.p8 by name in this directory and in ./private_keys. The .p8 downloads exactly once; a key generated and not downloaded is dead and must be revoked.
appStoreConnect.//backupPath: Copies of the .p8 files, kept out of any repo.

account.//: Account-level facts that the App Store Connect API does not expose, kept here so they are not re-derived from the browser every submission. Per-account, so a new project copies this block unchanged.
account.//type: Individual or Organization. An Individual account displays a personal name as the seller and there is no field anywhere that overrides it — the only route to a company seller line is converting to Organization, which requires a D-U-N-S number.
account.//address: The address on file for the developer account.
account.//traderStatus: EU Digital Services Act. Declaring trader status publishes this contact on the EU listing, so it must be a contact that can actually be reached.
account.//membershipPhone: What Membership Details carries. Prefer traderStatus.phone for App Review so the shipped app, the DSA record and the review contact all agree.
account.//dunsRequired: Needed only to convert to an Organization. Takes days to issue. Not a blocker for shipping.

review.//: App Review Information, which every version needs and which is per-account rather than per-app.
review.//contactEmail: Use the address that also appears on your privacy policy, so the reviewer's reply lands where the public contact does.
review.//demoAccount: This app has no accounts and no server. Leave sign-in-required UNCHECKED — checking it with blank credentials fails validation, and it is checked by default on some records.
review.//sellerName: What the App Store shows as the seller. This is the account's legal entity and is NOT free text: an Individual account displays a personal name, and showing a company requires converting to an Organization account with a D-U-N-S number.
review.//copyright: Free text, unlike sellerName. Format is 'YYYY Entity' — App Store Connect adds the copyright symbol itself.

listing.//: Defaults that held for the shipped app. Confirm per app; the point is to stop re-deciding them.
listing.//primaryLocale: Set at app creation and effectively permanent.
listing.//urls: Support and marketing URLs are required and are checked by the reviewer. A privacy policy URL is required for every app, with no exception for apps that collect nothing.
listing.//fieldLimits: Counted, not estimated — App Store Connect rejects on save with 'Must be less than N characters' and does not truncate. Name 30, subtitle 30, keywords 100 comma-separated with no spaces after commas, promotional text 170, description 4000, review notes 4000. Subtitle is indexed for search, so repeating a keyword there wastes it; competitor trademarks in any of these fields draw rejections.
listing.//copyright: Required for submission and easy to leave blank, since nothing prompts for it. Format is 'YYYY Entity' — App Store Connect adds the copyright symbol itself.
listing.//sku: Set once at app creation and read-only afterwards. It is internal and never shown to users, so a typo in it is permanent and harmless — but get it right, because it is the one identifier you cannot revise.
listing.//screenshots: web/press/ holds the curated set plus a manifest. scripts/media/prepare-screenshots.ts resizes raw captures to the sizes App Store Connect accepts; scripts/site/publish-press-kit.ts writes the manifest. Declaring iPad in TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY obliges iPad screenshots.

//: The marketing site in web/, built by scripts/site/site.ts and served by a
Cloudflare static-assets Worker. Nothing in the app depends on this block —
leave it as-is if you are only building and sideloading.
The Cloudflare credentials are not here. The account id lives in web/.env
(gitignored, see web/.env.example) and the API token is ambient — wrangler
reads both from the environment with no flags.
site.//origin: Canonical absolute origin. Goes into <link rel=canonical>, og:url and sitemap.xml, so it must be the domain you actually serve, not the workers.dev hostname.
site.//brand: The short wordmark in the header. Nine or fewer characters — the nav is nine items wide and a long brand wraps it.
site.//pages: Every page site.ts localises. A page missing from this list is still copied, but its cross-page links are NOT rewritten per locale — which silently drops translated readers onto the English version.
site.//workerName: `name` in web/wrangler.toml. Also the workers.dev subdomain.
site.//domains: Hostnames bound to the Worker as custom_domain routes. Cloudflare creates the DNS record itself — do not add one by hand, the two will fight.
site.//zone: The Cloudflare zone the domains above belong to.
//analyticsToken: Cloudflare Web Analytics site token, injected into every built page by scripts/site/site.ts. Not a secret — it ships in public HTML. A zone's automatic installation does NOT cover a Workers custom domain: it rewrites HTML at the edge and the Worker answers before that rewrite, so the beacon has to be in the page. Null disables the beacon.

tooling.//: Per-account rather than per-app; these rarely change between projects.
tooling.//xcodegen: project.yml is the source of truth and the .xcodeproj is generated and gitignored. Regenerate rather than editing the project file.
tooling.//upload: scripts/appstore/asc-upload.ts — reads this file, then uploads with asc builds upload. It refuses to upload when the local build number is not ahead of the one Apple already has, because a rejected upload still consumes the number.
tooling.//install: xcrun devicectl device install app --device <udid> <path>.app. `xcrun devicectl list devices` for the UDID. Fails with kAMDMobileImageMounterDeviceLocked if the device is locked.
tooling.//localize: Endpoint for scripts/lib/translator.ts, an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions server. Kept here rather than in the source so the repo names no host on anyone's LAN. Override per-run with LOCALIZE_URL. Only scripts/site/localize.ts uses it; the app does not.
